newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euroshares hit by poor Wall St start,politics.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euroshares hit by poor Wall St start,politics.

text.p: European bourses fell on Friday, dragged further down by a poor start on Wall Street and amid worries over political uncertainty in Britain and France.
On currency markets, the dollar weakened slightly against the yen as the suspension of a major Japanese insurer prompted speculation about higher interest rates in Tokyo.

London and Paris, both facing general elections in coming weeks, chalked up losses but Frankfurt suffered the most, its computerised IBIS index tumbling over one percent at one point on profit-taking.
"It's the end of the week, everyone's tired and wants to go home," said a dealer in London.
A weak opening on Wall Street -- it was down 0.5 percent in early trade -- and strong UK first quarter growth figures depressed London prices and added to concerns over near-term interest rate rises.
London's FTSE index fell 0.5 percent in early afternoon
amid a background of doubt over the outcome of May 1 elections in which the Conservative government is expected to be ousted by the opposition Labour party, according to opinion polls.
Dealers and strategists said Friday morning's GDP figures added more weight to the case for higher near-term interest rates. A rate rise soon after the poll is anticipated whoever comes to power.

"The figures mean four percent annualised growth which is pretty strong growth, well above trend and reinforces the likelihood of rate increases soon," said Credit Lyonnais Laing economist, Andrew Smith.
The Paris bourse made hefty losses in thin morning trade with many investors holding back amid election uncertainty, but recovered some poise later.
"We're waiting for the polls and for the election," one broker said. "The polls are being closely watched but they have a very short term impact.
An IPSOS poll showing the ruling conservative coalition would get a wafer-thin majority weighed on the French financial markets .

"Investors will steer clear until the election. The risk, in terms of market valuation, is too great. Better wait a month and find out what France's direction will be," said one trader. "Until then, we'll be driven by the polls."
Frankfurt had the worst day. Floor trade ended down 0.6 percent and dealings in the after-hours computerised IBIS index lost similar amounts as investors pocketed profits before the weekend.

Market interest focused on the construction sector after builders Holzmann AG and Hochtief AG both said they were pulling out of Germany's high-speed rail Transrapid project because of questions about the project's costs.

In currencies, the dollar was marginally stronger on the mark but slipped slightly against the yen, with dollar sentiment hit by a rise in Japanese market interest rates overnight because of renewed worries over Japan's financial industry.

The anxiety was prompted by the suspension of the big Japanese insurance company Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Company. This triggered concern that Nissan's foreign bonds would be liquidated, causing a large repatriation of funds.

But the slide was slight and the dollar was not expected to move greatly before the weekend meeting of finance ministers and central bankers from the G7 group of industrialised countries in Washington.

"The latest worries about Japan's financial system are a distraction for the market ahead of the G7, and the yen is a touch stronger as a result but the FX impact was marginal," said Roger Francis, senior analyst at IBJ International.
Traders will be keeping a close on eye on Friday's meeting in Washington between U.S. President Bill Clinton and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
STOCKS AT 1430 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was down 23.7 points at 4,364.8.
The Paris CAC-40 index fell 7.53 points at 2,532.79.
Frankfurt's DAX ended down 23.26 at 3,374.10.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7180 against the mark versus 1.7150 in late European trade on Thursday. Against the yen, the dollar was quoted at 125.73 from 125.90.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $342.25 an ounce after ending at $340.65 in London. Silver was at $4.74, two cents higher.
